# pvecli backup restore

Restore a backup as a new guest, or over a stopped one with --force.

```text
pvecli backup restore VOLID [OPTIONS]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `VOLID` | Backup volume, e.g. pbs:backup/vm/100/2026-11-18T02:00:00Z. |

## Options

| Option | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `-id`, `--vmid N` | Target ID (default: next free ID). |
| `-n`, `--node VALUE` | Node to restore on (default: where the backup or guest is). |
| `-s`, `--storage VALUE` | Target storage (VM default: from the backup; CT default: storage of its root disk). |
| `--start` | Start the guest once restored. |
| `--unique` | New random MAC addresses (the original may still run). |
| `-f`, `--force` | Overwrite an existing, stopped guest with this ID. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip confirmation. |
| `-p`, `--profile VALUE` | Profile to use. |

## Examples

```bash
pvecli backup restore local:backup/vzdump-qemu-100-2026_11_18-02_00_00.vma.zst
pvecli backup restore pbs:backup/ct/200/2026-11-18T02:00:00Z --vmid 905 --start
```
